title: Timeframes
hook: Higher timeframes tell the story. Lower timeframes let you step inside it.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain what actually changes when you switch timeframes — and what doesn't.

beats.heading: Views, not different markets
beats.body: The 1 minute, 5 minute, 1 hour, and 4 hour are not different markets — they are different views of the same price story.

beats.heading: Detail vs direction
beats.body: Lower timeframes show more detail. Higher timeframes show more direction.

blocks.heading: Zoom through the timeframes
blocks.prompt: Tap each lens to see how candle density changes at different zoom levels.

blocks.quote: Timeframes change your perspective on the same market. The market itself never changes just because you switched the chart view.

questions.question: What actually changes when you switch timeframes?
options: Your perspective on the same market
questions.why: Timeframe changes your view — the underlying price story stays the same.

questions.question: A trader checks the 1M chart first, decides it looks bullish, and takes a long without ever looking at the 4H. What is she missing?
options: The bigger-picture context the 4H would have given her
Nothing — the 1M is always sufficient on its own
The 1M is more reliable than any higher timeframe
questions.why: The 1M can look convincing while running counter to the larger story the 4H reveals.

takeaways: Every timeframe is a different zoom on the same price story.
Higher timeframes show direction; lower timeframes show detail.
Skipping the higher timeframe means trading without the bigger picture.
remember: The market doesn't change when you switch the chart view — your perspective does.
